meta.title: Loosen three checks that keep stopping agents, for 14 days, while a team fixes them?
meta.notice: Sample data for previewing the template. Every number on this page is illustrative.

recommendation.headline: I recommend loosening the three checks that only guard things git can restore and that the guard can switch, and keeping the four that guard money, messages, secrets and unbacked data.
recommendation.why: These checks stopped 31 runs and cost about 46 agent hours this week. A single agent can't overrule them, and shouldn't. From the portfolio view they look like immature parts of our own system, not real dangers.

source.label: Agent Manager blocked runs by check

blocked.title: Runs stopped by a check, each day for two weeks

groups.title: Guard only things git can restore

items.title: Agent identity check on code edits
items.text: Stops an agent whose identity token didn't reach its session.
items.worst: a wrong edit, restored from git

items.title: Approval must match the exact run
items.text: Your approval exists but is tied to a different run, so it's refused.
items.worst: an approved action runs in the wrong session

items.title: Sandbox blocks writes to the shared work tree
items.text: Agents work in one shared tree by design; the sandbox assumes separate copies.

items.title: Agents may only launch through Agent Manager
items.text: When Agent Manager is down, agents wait instead of using the coding agent CLI.
items.worst: a run Agent Manager doesn't track

items.title: Payments and purchases need your yes
items.text: Anything that spends or charges money.

items.title: Messages to people outside need your yes
Secrets and credentials
items.text: Reading or changing keys and passwords.

items.title: Deleting data outside the repo
items.text: Includes 59 GB of research with no backup yet.

steps.title: Fourteen days, then the checks come back fixed

items.text: The chosen checks switch to “log only”. Every action they would have stopped is still recorded.
The blocked jobs re-run. A fix team starts on each loosened check.
The briefing lists what got through that the checks would have stopped.
Checks return on their own, fixed. If a fix isn't ready, I ask before extending.

tripwire.text: If anything touches money, outside messages, secrets or data outside the repo, every loosened check snaps back at once and you get a notification.

options.title: Loosen for 14 days
bullets: Daily list of what got through

bullets: No return date; fixes still happen
You rely on git and reviews

options.title: Keep them; fix first
bullets: About 46 h a week stays lost
Agents keep stopping in the meantime

noAnswer.text: All checks stay as they are and keep stopping runs at about the same rate. I bring this to Tuesday's weekly review with one more week of evidence.
